operations.specification: Create a guest identity and return authorization tokens in a single public request. Validate the guest join payload, persist the guest record, and issue the authorized token response on success. Reject malformed input with validation errors and do not require an existing session or credentials.
operations.description:
Register a guest and issue authorization tokens.

This endpoint creates a temporary guest identity for an unauthenticated visitor in the private todo application and returns the authorized token payload needed for continued access. It is the guest entry point for starting an authenticated session without signing in as a registered member.

The request body must be validated strictly before any token is issued. Because guest access is temporary and token-based, the operation is public and does not depend on an existing account, profile, or session.

Use this endpoint as the first step in the guest authentication flow. Clients should store the returned tokens and later use the refresh endpoint to renew access when needed.

requestBody.description: Payload used to create a guest identity and begin a guest authorization session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after successful guest registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Validate the guest refresh token and issue a new authorized token payload if the token is valid. Reject expired, malformed, revoked, or otherwise invalid tokens with an unauthorized response. The operation should remain stateless aside from whatever token storage is needed to verify refresh validity.
operations.description:
Refresh guest authorization tokens.

This endpoint exchanges a valid guest refresh token for a new authorized token payload so a guest session can continue without creating a new guest identity. It is the renewal path for guest access in the private todo application.

The request body must include the refresh token, and the server must verify that it belongs to a valid guest authorization context before issuing new tokens. If validation fails, the request must be rejected as unauthorized.

Use this endpoint whenever guest access needs to be extended after the current token expires or is about to expire.

requestBody.description: Payload containing the guest refresh token used to obtain renewed authorization.

responseBody.description: Authorized token payload returned after a successful guest token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate the member sign-up payload, create the member account, initialize the authentication state required for token issuance, and return the authorized token bundle. Reject duplicate or invalid credentials without creating a partial account.
operations.description:
Create a new member account and return authorization tokens.

This endpoint registers a private app member using the required sign-up credentials and returns the authorized token payload on success. It is the entry point for first-time access to the authenticated todo area and establishes the member identity used for profile, todo, trash, and history operations.

The request body must match the member join contract exactly. If the submitted credentials are invalid or already in use, the request must fail without creating a partial account. On success, the response returns the authorized authentication payload for the newly created member.

requestBody.description: Member registration credentials for creating a new authenticated account.

responseBody.description: Authorized authentication payload returned after successful member registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Verify the member's credentials against the stored account record, issue fresh authentication tokens on success, and reject invalid credentials without revealing whether the email exists. Ensure the response contains the standard authorized token bundle only after successful password verification.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing member and return authorization tokens.

This endpoint validates the member's login credentials and issues the authorized token payload needed to access private todo features. It is used by returning users who already have an account and need a new authenticated session.

If the credentials are invalid, the operation must fail with an authentication error and must not reveal whether the email address is registered. On success, the response contains the standard authorized authentication payload for the member.

requestBody.description: Member login credentials used to authenticate an existing account.

responseBody.description: Authorized authentication payload returned after successful member login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the refresh token, confirm it belongs to an active member session, and issue a new authorized token bundle. Reject expired, malformed, revoked, or mismatched tokens. If the implementation stores session state, use it to prevent token reuse.
operations.description:
Refresh the member's authorization tokens.

This endpoint exchanges a valid refresh token for a new authorized token payload so the member can continue using the private todo application without re-entering credentials. It is part of the standard token renewal flow for authenticated members.

The request body must match the member refresh contract exactly. If the token is invalid, expired, revoked, or no longer tied to an active session, the request must fail without issuing new tokens. On success, the response returns the updated authorized authentication payload for the member.

requestBody.description: Member token refresh payload used to renew an active authentication session.

responseBody.description: Authorized authentication payload returned after successful token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Delete the signed-in member's own account.

This endpoint is available only to the authenticated owner of the account. It removes the active member account and performs the required cleanup of the owner’s private profile and todos, including todos that are already in the trash.

The application is private, so the target account is always the current session holder. Requests for any other account must be rejected, and deleted accounts must not remain usable for future access or sign-in.

The underlying member record is stored with a unique email address, a password hash, and lifecycle timestamps. Those stored fields are managed internally and are not exposed by this endpoint.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Authenticate the request using the current member session and verify that the caller is the account owner before taking any action. Reject unauthenticated requests and any request that does not belong to the active member.

Execute the deletion as a single transactional account-lifecycle operation. Remove the member record and permanently remove the member's private profile and all todos owned by that member, including todos currently in trash. Ensure dependent todo edit history records are also removed so no orphaned private data remains after account deletion.

Do not return member identity, credential, or timestamp data in the response. The endpoint should succeed with no content or a minimal confirmation body if the service convention requires one; for this operation, no response body is needed.

requestBody.description: Request body for deleting the signed-in member's own account. No additional account identifier is required because the current authenticated session determines the target account.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's private account record.

This operation returns the account identity data for one member only, using the unique account identifier in the path. The account belongs to a single person and is part of the private todo application boundary.

Only the owning authenticated member may access this resource. The service must not expose other users' account information, and it must not return accounts that have been deleted. If the account does not exist, is deleted, or does not belong to the requester, the service must return the appropriate not-found or forbidden response according to the application's error handling policy.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Fetch the todo_app_members record by id and verify that it belongs to the authenticated caller. Reject access when the requested account id does not match the caller's account or when deleted_at is set. Return the full member entity contract for the API, but never expose the raw password_hash in the serialized response. Preserve the private-account boundary and use the account's unique UUID as the lookup key. If no accessible record is found, respond with the standard not-found or forbidden error used by the service.

responseBody.description: The authenticated member's account record.

parameters.description: The unique UUID of the member account to retrieve in global scope.
parameters.name: accountId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member account.

This endpoint lets a member modify their own account identity in the private todo application. The service must verify that the account identified by the path parameter belongs to the current authenticated member before applying any changes.

Only member-account fields may be processed here. The profile display name belongs to the separate profile entity and is not updated by this operation. If the requested email conflicts with another member account, or if the request targets another user's account, the service must reject the request with an appropriate error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Load the todo_app_members row by id and verify that it belongs to the authenticated requester. Reject the request if the member does not exist, is deleted, or is not owned by the current member. Apply only supported account-level fields from the update payload, specifically the fields defined by the member schema. Enforce the unique email constraint before persisting email changes. If the password is updated, hash the new password before storing it in password_hash and never persist raw credentials. Update updated_at on successful persistence. Do not touch todo_app_profiles in this operation. Return not found or forbidden-style errors for missing records or ownership violations, and conflict errors for duplicate email values.

responseBody.description: The updated member account record after a successful update.

parameters.description: The UUID of the member account to update in private account scope.
parameters.name: accountId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the authenticated member account.

operations.description:
Returns the authenticated member's session records.

This endpoint lets a signed-in member browse their own login sessions in a paginated list. Each result represents a session record stored for security and auditing purposes, including the member reference, IP address, request URL, referrer URL, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp.

The service must scope every query to the current authenticated member and must not expose any session that belongs to another member. Session validity and expiration rules should be enforced consistently when assembling the result set, and invalid search or pagination input should be rejected as a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_member_sessions using the authenticated member id from the security context and never accept a member id from the request body. Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request DTO. Default ordering should be newest first by created_at unless overridden.

Use the schema columns exactly as stored: id, todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at. Return only a summary projection suitable for list browsing. Do not expose any secret token value because none exists in the schema. Reject unauthorized access, expired sessions in an unauthenticated context, and malformed list parameters with the appropriate auth or validation error.

responseBody.description: Paginated session summaries for the authenticated member.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for the authenticated member's session list.

operations.description:
Retrieve a member session by its UUID identifier.

This endpoint returns the stored session record for a single logged-in member, including the owning member reference and the audit metadata captured when the session was issued. It is intended for session inspection and security-related workflows that need to verify a specific session instance.

The returned data includes the owning member reference, the source IP address, the request URL, the referrer URL, the creation timestamp, and the expiration timestamp. If the session does not exist, the service must return a not found error. Callers must only be able to access sessions they are authorized to inspect.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load todo_app_member_sessions by primary key id and return the matching row. Validate that sessionId is a UUID and return 404 when no session exists.

Do not mutate the session record, refresh expiration, or trigger logout behavior. Preserve the stored ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at values as-is. If authorization is enforced at this layer, verify the caller may inspect the requested session before returning the entity.

responseBody.description: The full session record for the requested identifier, including the member relationship and audit metadata.

parameters.description: The UUID of the session to retrieve.
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Reset a member account password using a valid recovery token.

The service must resolve the supplied token against the password reset records, ensure it is still valid, and then update the password credential for the linked member account. The reset applies only to the owning account and must not change email, ownership, or account lifecycle data.

If the token is unknown, expired, already consumed, or does not belong to an existing member, the request must be rejected. On success, the new password replaces the previous password hash for future sign-in attempts, and the reset record should be invalidated so it cannot be reused.
operations.name: reset
operations.specification:
Look up the password reset request by its unique token in todo_app_member_password_resets. Reject the request when the token is missing, invalid, expired, deleted, or not linked to an existing member. Validate the new password against the account password policy before hashing it.

Update todo_app_members.password_hash for the linked member in the same transaction as invalidating the reset record. If the schema supports deleted_at-based invalidation for reset records, set deleted_at on successful consumption; otherwise, use the service's existing consumption logic without inventing new fields. Do not alter member email, created_at, deleted_at, or any unrelated account fields. Return the updated member entity without exposing password_hash.

responseBody.description: The member account after the password credential has been successfully replaced.

requestBody.description: The password reset token and the new password to apply to the linked account.

operations.description:
Retrieve a password reset request by its identifier.

This endpoint returns the full password reset record associated with the supplied reset identifier, including the linked member reference, reset token, expiration time, and audit timestamps. It is intended for password recovery and security workflows that need to inspect a single reset request record.

The record belongs to exactly one member account through the todo_app_member_id relation. If the identifier does not exist, or the record is no longer available, the request should be rejected with a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Load the todo_app_member_password_resets row by id and return it only when it exists. If needed for ownership context, join the related todo_app_members row through todo_app_member_id, but do not expose any member fields unless the response schema explicitly includes them. Return the actual stored columns only: id, todo_app_member_id, token, expired_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Do not invent password fields, because this table stores reset requests rather than password credentials. Treat unavailable records as not found.

responseBody.description: The full password reset request record for the specified identifier.

parameters.description: The password reset request identifier (global scope).
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member’s own private profile.

This endpoint returns only the profile record that belongs to the current signed-in account. The profile is account-linked and private, so the response is limited to the member’s own display name record and does not expose any other user’s profile data.

Use this operation when the UI needs to display the member’s profile label. If the caller is not authenticated, the member account is inactive, or the profile cannot be resolved for the current account, the request must fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found response used by the service layer.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Fetch the profile row associated with the current authenticated member from todo_app_profiles using the active session’s member identity. Enforce ownership through the session context, and do not accept a path parameter because this resource always represents the caller’s own profile.

Return only the profile fields stored in the table and never expose credential data or another user’s profile. If the request is unauthenticated, the member is deleted/inactive, or the profile is inaccessible for the current account, return the corresponding authorization or not-found error.

responseBody.description: The authenticated member’s private profile record, including the display name.

operations.description:
Update the current member's profile display name.

This operation updates only the authenticated member's own profile and is limited to the display name field. The profile remains private to the owning member, and the request must not target any other user's profile.

If the display name is invalid or unchanged, the request must be rejected. No other profile attributes are in scope for this operation. On success, the response returns the updated profile so the client can immediately show the member's current identity label in the app.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member from the current session and load that member's profile record. Apply an update only to the display_name column, and reject any request body properties other than displayName.

Validate the new display name according to the profile rules and business requirements, including rejecting empty or blank values. If the new value matches the existing display name, return a validation error because the update must change the display name in this unit. Preserve the private ownership boundary by never allowing a profile identifier to be provided in the path or request body. Persist the change in a single profile update and return the updated profile entity.

responseBody.description: The updated private profile for the signed-in member after the display name change is saved.

requestBody.description: The new display name for the current member's own profile. No other profile fields are allowed.

operations.description:
Create a new private todo for the authenticated member.

The caller submits the todo fields that define the new item, including the required title and the optional description, start date, and due date. The service assigns ownership from the current session, stores the record as incomplete by default, and returns the created todo.

Validation follows the todo business rules: title is required, optional fields must satisfy their own constraints, and the request must not include any owner identifier. Access is limited to signed-in members, and invalid input must be rejected before any record is created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a record in todo_app_todos using the authenticated member as the owner. Resolve the owner from the security context and never trust or accept ownership fields from the client. Validate the required title and the optional description, start date, and due date according to the todo rules. Set the initial completion state to incomplete. Do not create a todo edit history entry for initial creation. Return the persisted todo after insertion. Enforce authorization so only signed-in members can call this endpoint, and surface validation errors without persisting partial data.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo with its persisted fields and current completion state.

requestBody.description: The fields required to create a new todo for the authenticated member.

operations.description:
Returns a paginated list of the authenticated member's own todos.

This endpoint is used to browse the normal todo list. It supports completion-status filtering, sorting by creation date, start date, or due date, and excludes todos that have been moved out of the normal list.

Each item contains the fields needed for a list view, including title, completion status, start date, due date, and creation date. Full details and edit history are intentionally not included here.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the todo_app_todos table for the authenticated member only. Apply ownership filtering using the current member identity and exclude records that are not in the normal list state. Support completion-status filtering with the allowed values all, complete, and incomplete. Support sorting by creation date, start date, and due date, with explicit handling so rows missing start date or due date are placed at the end when those sort keys are selected. Implement stable pagination and return total-count metadata. Reject invalid filter or sort values with a validation error. Never expose another member's todos.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries for the authenticated member's normal todo list.

requestBody.description: Pagination, completion-status filter, and sorting options for browsing the authenticated member's todo list.

operations.description:
Returns a single todo owned by the current member.

This endpoint fetches one todo by its UUID and returns the full record needed for a detail screen, including title, description, start date, due date, completion state, and audit timestamps. The todo must belong to the authenticated member, and records owned by another member or marked as deleted are not returned.

This is a private member-only operation. It does not expose other members, profiles, or shared data, and it should respond with a not-found style error when the requested todo is unavailable to the current member.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos by id and the authenticated member id so the read is ownership-scoped. Return the full row with id, todo_app_member_id, title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

If no row matches, if the row belongs to another member, or if deleted_at is not null, return a not-found response. Do not join unrelated tables. Do not leak whether another member owns the record. Map the successful result to the full Todo DTO used by the API layer.

responseBody.description: The full todo record for the authenticated member’s detail view.

parameters.description: The todo UUID in global scope.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Update one of the current member's own todos.

This endpoint allows an authenticated member to change the title, description, start date, and due date of a single todo. The todo must belong to the current member, and the service must reject attempts to edit another user's record.

When the update succeeds, the todo is saved and a corresponding edit history entry is recorded. The response returns the full updated todo so clients can refresh the detail view or list display immediately.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Fetch the target todo from todo_app_todos using todoId and verify that it belongs to the authenticated member. If the record does not exist or is not owned by the current member, return an access or not-found error and do not write any history.

Accept updates only for the mutable todo fields: title, description, start date, and due date. Apply partial updates by keeping existing values for omitted fields. Validate all provided values according to the todo rules, including the required title constraint and date handling rules.

Persist the todo update and create a matching row in todo_app_todo_edit_histories within the same transaction. The history row should capture the edit event and the new values for any fields that changed. Do not alter completion state, ownership, or any deleted/trash state in this operation.

Return the updated todo after the transaction commits.

responseBody.description: The updated todo with its current field values after the edit has been applied.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo to update.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: The editable todo fields for an update request. Provide the values you want to change; omitted fields remain unchanged.

operations.description:
Move one of the authenticated member's todos to trash.

This operation marks the specified todo as deleted instead of removing it permanently. The todo must belong to the requesting member, and the service must prevent access to any other user's todo. After deletion, the todo is removed from the normal todo list and becomes available in the trash list until it is restored or permanently deleted.

If the todo does not exist, does not belong to the current member, or is already unavailable for deletion, the request must fail with an appropriate client error without exposing another user's data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Fetch the target todo by todoId and verify that it is owned by the authenticated member before applying any change. If the record is missing or the owner does not match, reject the request using the application's ownership error policy without disclosing another user's data.

Implement deletion as a trash transition rather than a physical delete. Update the todo's deletion state so normal todo list queries exclude it and trash queries can include it. Preserve the todo record and its edit history for restore and permanent-trash-delete workflows.

Do not change unrelated fields such as title, description, dates, or completion state. If the todo is already deleted, return a domain-appropriate client error. Perform the state change in a transaction if the implementation later adds side effects.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo to move to trash, scoped to the authenticated member's own todos.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's trashed todos in a paginated list.

This endpoint returns only todos that belong to the current member and are currently in the trash. It supports browsing large trash sets through pagination, and it can be used together with completion-status filters and sort options to help members find deleted todos quickly.

Only summary fields suitable for list display should be returned. The list must never include active todos or any data owned by other members. Deleted todos remain recoverable until they are restored or permanently removed through the dedicated trash actions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_todos table for rows owned by the authenticated member and marked as deleted/trash according to the application's trash state handling. Exclude all non-trashed todos.

Apply pagination from the request body and return a paginated result set sorted according to the requested sort order. Support completion-status filtering for all, complete only, or incomplete only trashed todos if the request DTO includes those fields. For date-based sorting, ensure todos with null start date or due date are placed at the end when sorting by that field, matching the business rules.

Select only list-safe columns for the summary projection. Do not join or expose other members' data. If the member has no trashed todos, return an empty page with valid pagination metadata. Authorization must require an authenticated member context; unauthenticated access should be rejected by the auth layer before query execution.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of trashed todo summaries owned by the current member.

requestBody.description: Trash list search criteria including pagination, completion-status filtering, and sort options for the current member's deleted todos.

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo back to the active list.

This operation is available only to the owning member and only for a todo that is currently in trash. When restoration succeeds, the todo becomes visible again in the normal todo list while keeping its existing completion status.

Ownership and lifecycle rules are enforced strictly. Requests for another member's todo, for a todo that is not deleted, or for a todo that has already been permanently removed must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the todo by id and verify that it belongs to the current authenticated member. Reject the request if the todo does not exist, belongs to another member, or is not currently soft-deleted.

On success, clear the deleted_at value so the todo returns to the active list. Preserve all other todo fields, especially is_completed, title, description, start_date, due_date, created_at, and updated_at semantics. Update the modified timestamp as part of the restore workflow if the service convention requires it.

Do not create or modify any todo edit history records during restore. If the todo has been permanently deleted, return a not-found or invalid-state style error consistent with the service conventions.

responseBody.description: The restored todo record after it has been returned to the active list.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo to restore within the authenticated member's own todo collection.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Permanently deletes one of the authenticated member's todos.

This operation removes the selected todo from the application and is intended for items that are already in trash. The todo must belong to the current member; attempts to access another user's todo are rejected.

When the todo is removed, its edit history entries are also removed through the database relationship. After deletion, the todo is no longer available in the normal todo list, trash view, or history views.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Verify the authenticated caller is a member and load the target todo by id with ownership enforcement using todo_app_todos.id and todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id.
Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden style error when the todo does not exist or does not belong to the current member.
Only allow this operation for a todo that is being permanently removed; do not perform a status update or move it back to active state.
Delete the todo row permanently from todo_app_todos. The associated todo_app_todo_edit_histories rows must be removed automatically by the existing cascade relation on todo_app_todo_histories.todo_app_todo_id -> todo_app_todos.id.
Do not return edit history data. Ensure the deletion is idempotent from a privacy perspective: after successful deletion the todo must not appear in any list, trash, or detail lookup.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo to permanently delete (UUID scope within the authenticated member's own data).
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Lists the edit history entries for a specific todo owned by the current member.

This operation returns the history records associated with the requested todo, ordered from the most recent change to the oldest by default. The history is private to the todo owner and must not expose records belonging to another member's todos.

The response is paginated for browsing in the UI. Each item represents one successful edit and reflects the changed todo values captured for that revision, such as title, description, start date, and due date when those fields were modified.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Verify that the authenticated member owns the todo identified by todoId before querying history. If the todo does not exist or is not owned by the current member, return a not-found style response to avoid leaking cross-user existence.

Query todo_app_todo_edit_histories by the todo foreign key, and sort the records by the edit timestamp descending so the newest change appears first. Apply pagination from the request body. If the request includes additional filtering or search criteria supported by the IRequest contract, apply them after scoping to the todo.

Do not include histories for todos that belong to other users. Do not expose internal identifiers or unrelated todo data in the list response. The endpoint should return a paginated summary shape suitable for list screens.

responseBody.description: Paginated edit history summaries for the requested todo, ordered from newest to oldest.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo whose edit history will be listed.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination and search criteria for browsing a todo's edit history entries.

prerequisites.description: A todo must exist before its edit history can be listed, because edit history entries belong to a specific parent todo.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single edit history entry for one of your todos.

This endpoint returns the immutable history row for the specified todo and edit history identifiers, including the time of the edit and the values that were changed in that revision. It is intended for viewing the full change record of a private todo, not for modifying history data.

Access is limited to the signed-in member who owns the parent todo. The server must verify that the edit history row belongs to the requested todo and that the todo belongs to the current member before returning the record. If either identifier does not match an accessible record, the request must fail with a not-found or forbidden-style error as appropriate.

The response mirrors the stored history columns: edited_at, title, description, start_date, due_date, and created_at. Fields that were not changed in that edit may be null.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the todo by id and confirm it belongs to the current member. Then load the edit history row by id with an additional predicate that it belongs to the same todo id.

Return the full row directly from todo_app_todo_edit_histories. Use UUID path parameters for both todoId and editHistoryId. Do not accept a request body.

If the todo does not belong to the current member, return a not-found or forbidden response according to the existing authorization strategy. If the edit history is missing or is not attached to that todo, return not found. No joins are required for the payload itself because the edit history entity already contains all fields needed by the consumer.

responseBody.description: The full edit history record for the requested todo.

parameters.description: The identifier of the todo that owns the edit history entry (UUID).
parameters.name: todoId

parameters.description: The identifier of the edit history entry within the specified todo (UUID).
parameters.name: editHistoryId

prerequisites.description: The parent todo must exist before a specific edit-history entry can be retrieved under it, because the lookup is scoped by todoId and the server validates ownership of that todo first.

authorizations.name: guest
authorizations.description: Unauthenticated visitors who can sign up or log in.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated users who can manage only their own profile, todos, trash, and edit history.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
